title: Hearing the Basie band, its members and Jack Washington
summary: Tate hears the band play a dance and discusses Freddie Green, Shad Collins and Jack Washington.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I'll tell you later on what happened in Philadelphia. So anyway, that night, I went down and listened to him play the colored dance and I went down and listened to that band. Boy, phew. And something says, "Well, maybe you better go on back to Nat Tole." You know, I says, "Shith --" (Laughter.)
Whee, Joe was in good shape then and Joe was terrible when he used to play good, you know what I mean? He used to push that band, boy, right on in. And then, boy, they --
Was Freddie Green with the band then?
Yeah. Freddie, Earl, Jack Washington, Buck, Sweets, Dickie Well, Shad Collins was playing his ass off.
What kind of player was Washington as a soloist?
Ooh, baritone player, man, he was something. Gerry Mulligan loves him. He said that's who he really loved.
Not enough. Basie was like that. He did more -- of course, when he was with Bennie Moten, Bennie Moten featured him all the time. But Basie never featured him. Now, listen to "Dogging Around," --

-- and "Topsy," Basie's "Topsy." Listen, make a special notice to listen to his baritone playing on that. And -- oh, I can think of some more. I can't think of them all now. But those are the things where he had a chance to really stretch out. Oh, man, he's a fantastic baritone. But Basie's a kind of funny guy. He'll feature one man all night, you know, sometimes. Then the next night, he might feature the other guy all night.
Did Jack stay with Basie until the end?
No, Jack -- he went in the Army. Let's see, Jack went in the Army, he was inducted in the Army. Did he come back to the band after that? I believe he came back

to the band after his stint in the Army. Then when did he leave? I'm trying to remember if Jack was with the band when it broke up. See, I stayed with the band until the band really broke up, the first band. And then he had a quartet. Then when he went out and organized again, I couldn't make it. I stayed here in New York. I was getting my 802 card and I was recording like two and three times a day. You know, I didn't know it was so nice here in New York, you know, because I'd been on the road, you know. I'll tell you about that.
